title: SLO-led memory packing and tenant fairness for continuous batching
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: continuous batching on shared GPUs leads to imbalanced tenant outcomes when KV cache pressure and memory fragmentation interact with SLO-driven preemption. We need a planner that packs KV and activation memory across concurrent slices, enforces SLOs at request-level, and yields fair preemption behavior so latency-sensitive tenants aren't starved by throughput-heavy tenants.

Goal: deliver an SLO-aware memory packing and eviction planner that: (1) accounts for live KV residency and ephemeral activation footprints, (2) computes per-tenant soft-reserves and reclaim priorities, (3) integrates with the existing continuous batcher to apply graceful suspend/resume where needed, and (4) exposes conservative telemetry for canary rollout.

Why now: recent production incidents showed 2x P95 spikes for low-priority tenants during mixed workloads with long KV tails. Improving packing and preemption fairness reduces tail latency regressions and overall token-unit cost by avoiding unnecessary cold-KV thrashing.
updates: 2026-03-01: Scoped requirements with PM — agreed to target P95 and P99 SLO band for latency-sensitive routes; medium-priority background jobs get best-effort throughput.
2026-03-03: Spike completed — microbenchmarks on G5 cluster show KV-aware packing reduces peak allocation by ~18% vs baseline naive allocation for mixed long/short seq workloads.

2026-03-05: Design review with Storage and Runtime teams — two approaches proposed: (A) soft-reserve + rolling eviction order (tenant-weighted LRU), (B) slotized packing with cold-KV grace windows. Storage prefers (B) for predictability; runtime prefers (A) for simpler integration. Decided to prototype (A) first and measure.

2026-03-08: Prototype implemented in GKE dev cluster branch feature/eng-404210-packing — includes per-tenant KV accounting and a soft-reserve reclaim API. Initial chaos test: eviction occurred but cold-KV preservation thresholds prevented a full tail spike; P95 reduced by ~12%.

2026-03-10: Code review feedback (PR #2719) requested clearer invariants for resume: the batcher must not resume a preempted slice until necessary KV pages are hydrated or a fallback model variant is selected.
2026-03-12: Added task list and acceptance criteria; scheduling implementation for canary rollout in staging next week.
acceptance_criteria: Attach per-tenant memory accounting to all continuous-batch leases in the runtime and expose metrics (kv_resident_bytes, activation_bytes, soft_reserve_bytes)
Eviction planner computes reclaim score that combines SLO weight, KV recency, and tenant soft-reserve debt; reclaim order must be deterministic and explainable in logs
When under pressure, planner can trigger graceful suspend of lowest-priority slices with a documented handoff (KV checkpoint/mark) to enable later resume without full cold-KV penalty

End-to-end e2e benchmarks: mixed workload (50% short chat, 30% long chat, 20% background batch) must show <=10% regression in aggregate throughput and >15% improvement in 95th latency for latency-sensitive tenants compared to baseline
Canary rollout in staging with runtime-1.19 flag gated and dashboard showing tenant-level SLO delta, KV churn, and cold-KV miss rate
technical_notes:
Algorithm sketch:
1) Maintain per-lease accounting: kv_resident_estimate (bytes), activation_reserve_estimate (bytes), and recent_kv_access_score (decayed recency).
2) Soft-reserve: compute a target reserve per tenant = base_reserve + slo_weight * util_factor; base_reserve derived from historical working set percentiles.
3) Reclaim score = alpha * (soft_reserve_deficit / soft_reserve) + beta * (1 - recent_kv_access_score) + gamma * tenant_priority_penalty. Tune alpha/beta/gamma via offline sim.
4) Eviction action choices: evict cold KV pages, compress/quantize activation buffers, or preempt slice (mark for suspend). Prefer eviction or compression first if predicted resume cost < preemption cost.
5) Packing: use slab-style allocator for KV blocks to reduce fragmentation; allocate contiguous slabs per-tenant when possible and enable opportunistic compaction during low utilization windows.
6) Integration points: batcher admission -> ask planner for projected memory headroom; on admit, planner reserves soft-reserve; on pressure, runtime calls planner.reclaim() to obtain ordered reclaimables with suggested action and confidence score.
7) Observability: log deterministic reclaim decisions with the contributing score components; emit metrics for cold_kv_miss_ratio and preempt_resume_success_rate.

Performance trade-offs considered: tighter soft-reserves reduce cold-KV misses but increase latency for bursty tenants. Slab allocator improves fragmentation but adds background compaction CPU. We will gate compaction and use it in low-util periods only.

Implementation risk: inaccurate kv_resident_estimate leading to oscillation. Mitigation: conservative initial tuning + safety clamp to avoid >15% sudden preemptions in a 5m window.
tasks: Add per-lease KV and activation accounting hooks in the runtime (ENG changes)
Implement reclaim scoring module and unit tests for deterministic ordering
Wire soft-reserve allocation into admission flow and batcher state transitions
Add slab allocator prototype for KV blocks with optional compaction path
Create canary feature flag and staging job to exercise mixed workloads
Build Grafana dashboard: tenant SLO delta, kv_churn, cold_kv_miss_rate, preempt_count
Benchmarking: run standard mixed workload harness and record P50/P95/P99 and memory headroom curves
PRs: open RFC PR for design; implement code PRs and address code review feedback
